title: Luke Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 20.

questions.question: In Luke 20, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus taught the people in the temple
Jesus told the parable of the vineyard
Jesus asked about the baptism of John
The husbandmen killed the beloved son
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus taught the people in the temple
questions.explanation: Luke 20:1 states that Jesus was teaching the people in the temple before any other event mentioned.

questions.question: Who came upon Jesus while he was teaching in the temple according to Luke 20?
options: The chief priests, scribes, and elders
questions.correctAnswer: The chief priests, scribes, and elders
questions.explanation: Luke 20:1 states that the chief priests and scribes came upon Jesus with the elders.

questions.question: What question did the chief priests and scribes ask Jesus in Luke 20?
options: By what authority doest thou these things?
Who is the greatest in the kingdom of God?
questions.correctAnswer: By what authority doest thou these things?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:2 records them asking Jesus, 'Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things?'

questions.question: What did Jesus ask the chief priests and scribes about John’s baptism?
options: Was it from heaven or of men?
Was it for repentance or for forgiveness?
Was it performed in the Jordan or in Jerusalem?
Was it done with water or with fire?
questions.correctAnswer: Was it from heaven or of men?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:4 records Jesus asking, 'The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?'

questions.question: What reason did the chief priests and scribes give for not answering Jesus about John's baptism?
options: They said they could not tell whence it was
They said it was from heaven
They said it was from men
They said John was not a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: They said they could not tell whence it was
questions.explanation: Luke 20:7 states that they answered Jesus by saying they could not tell where John's baptism was from.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about telling them by what authority he did these things?
options: My authority is from the Father
questions.explanation: Luke 20:8 records Jesus saying, 'Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.'

questions.question: In the parable Jesus told, what did the certain man plant?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:9 states, 'A certain man planted a vineyard.'

questions.question: What did the man do with the vineyard after planting it?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:9 says the man let the vineyard forth to husbandmen.

questions.question: What happened to the first servant sent by the owner to the husbandmen?
options: They beat him and sent him away empty
They welcomed him and gave him fruit
They took him as a partner
questions.correctAnswer: They beat him and sent him away empty
questions.explanation: Luke 20:10 states the servant was beaten and sent away empty by the husbandmen.

questions.question: What did the husbandmen do to the third servant sent by the lord of the vineyard?
options: They wounded him and cast him out
questions.correctAnswer: They wounded him and cast him out
questions.explanation: Luke 20:12 says the third servant was wounded and cast out by the husbandmen.

questions.question: Who did the lord of the vineyard decide to send after the servants?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:13 states that the lord said, 'I will send my beloved son.'

questions.question: True or False: The husbandmen killed the beloved son of the lord of the vineyard.
questions.explanation: Luke 20:15 states that the husbandmen cast out and killed the beloved son.

questions.question: True or False: The lord of the vineyard said he would destroy the husbandmen and give the vineyard to others.
questions.explanation: Luke 20:16 states the lord will come, destroy the husbandmen, and give the vineyard to others.

questions.question: True or False: The text says that the husbandmen repented after Jesus told the parable.
questions.explanation: There is no mention in Luke 20:1-16 about the husbandmen repenting.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that the beloved son was welcomed by the husbandmen.
questions.explanation: Luke 20:14-15 says the husbandmen planned to kill and then killed the beloved son, not welcomed him.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say the stone which the builders rejected has become?
questions.explanation: This is correct as it directly quotes Luke 20:17, where Jesus refers to the stone becoming the head of the corner.

questions.question: What does Luke 20:25 promise will happen if someone renders to God the things that are God's?
questions.explanation: While Luke 20:25 discusses rendering to Caesar, it implies that honoring God brings blessings as a principle.

questions.question: What did the chief priests and scribes seek to do to Jesus after he spoke the parable?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:19 states that they sought to lay hands on him, fearing the people for his words.

questions.question: According to Luke 20:20, why did they send spies to watch Jesus?
options: To find fault in his words
questions.correctAnswer: To find fault in his words
questions.explanation: Luke 20:20 explains that they sent spies to take hold of his words, intending to deliver him to authority.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when he said, 'Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken'?
questions.explanation: This reflects the idea in Luke 20:18 that humility and acknowledgment of Christ lead to brokenness.

questions.question: What did Jesus ask them to show him to illustrate his point about tribute?
questions.explanation: In Luke 20:24, Jesus asks to show him a penny, which he uses to teach about tribute to Caesar.

questions.question: What did the Sadducees deny according to Luke 20:27?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:27 clearly states that the Sadducees deny that there is any resurrection.

questions.question: According to Luke 20:26, what was the reaction of the people to Jesus' answer?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:26 indicates that the people marveled at his answer and held their peace.

questions.question: What was the content of the question posed to Jesus about tribute in Luke 20:22?
options: Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?
Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar?
Is it lawful to forgive sins?
Is it lawful to eat with sinners?
questions.correctAnswer: Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:22 directly states that they asked if it was lawful to give tribute unto Caesar.

questions.question: What did Jesus imply about authority in response to the chief priests' question?
options: It is only for the righteous
questions.explanation: This reflects Jesus' teaching that authority comes from God, though he does not explicitly state it in Luke 20:8.

questions.question: According to Luke 20:31, what happened to the woman after all seven brothers died?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:32 states that last of all, the woman died also, completing the Sadducees' question.

questions.question: What does Luke 20:25 teach about our obligations to earthly authorities?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:25 teaches that we should render unto Caesar what is Caesar's, implying we have obligations.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus accepted the person of any when he taught?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:21 states that Jesus did not accept the person of any but taught the way of God truly.

questions.question: Is it false that the chief priests and scribes were indifferent to Jesus' words?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:19 shows that they feared the people and sought to lay hands on him because of his parable.

questions.question: Is it false that the Sadducees believed in the resurrection?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:27 states specifically that the Sadducees deny that there is any resurrection.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 20.

questions.question: In the resurrection, whose wife will the woman be, according to Luke 20:33?
options: For seven had her to wife.
She will be given to another.
questions.correctAnswer: For seven had her to wife.
questions.explanation: This question reflects the Sadducees' inquiry about the woman who had seven husbands. Luke 20:33 states, 'Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them is she? for seven had her to wife.'

questions.question: What did Jesus say about marriage in the resurrection in Luke 20:35?
options: They shall be given in marriage.
Neither marry nor are given in marriage.
questions.correctAnswer: Neither marry nor are given in marriage.
questions.explanation: In Luke 20:35, Jesus clarifies that those accounted worthy of resurrection 'neither marry, nor are given in marriage.'

questions.question: According to Luke 20:36, who are the children of God?
options: Those who are equal unto the angels.
questions.correctAnswer: Those who are equal unto the angels.
questions.explanation: Luke 20:36 states that 'they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.'

questions.question: What does Jesus reference to show that the dead are raised in Luke 20:37?
questions.explanation: In Luke 20:37, Jesus points to Moses at the bush as evidence for the resurrection, highlighting that 'he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'

questions.question: According to Luke 20:38, how does Jesus describe God?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:38 emphasizes that God 'is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.'

questions.question: What did the scribes say after Jesus answered them in Luke 20:39?
questions.explanation: In Luke 20:39, certain scribes replied, 'Master, thou hast well said,' indicating their agreement with Jesus' response.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'resurrection' (anastasis) in Luke 20:35 mean?
options: A rising up or standing up.
questions.correctAnswer: A rising up or standing up.
questions.explanation: 'Anastasis' in Luke 20:35 refers to the act of rising up, emphasizing the concept of resurrection as a restoration to life.

questions.question: What literary device is employed in Jesus' question about David's son in Luke 20:41?
questions.explanation: In Luke 20:41, Jesus poses a rhetorical question to challenge the understanding of the Messiah's lineage, emphasizing his authority.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of resurrection found in Luke 20:37?
questions.explanation: Exodus 3:6 recounts God's declaration to Moses, affirming the existence of the patriarchs, thus connecting to the resurrection theme in Luke 20:37.

questions.question: Which verse in the New Testament echoes the idea of God being a God of the living in Luke 20:38?
questions.explanation: In John 11:25, Jesus states, 'I am the resurrection, and the life,' affirming the belief in God as a God of the living, similar to Luke 20:38.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Luke 20:37?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:36 precedes Luke 20:37, where Jesus explains that those worthy of resurrection cannot die anymore.

questions.question: What comes immediately after Luke 20:46?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:47 follows Luke 20:46, where Jesus warns about the scribes' behavior and their greater damnation.

questions.question: In Luke 20:44, Jesus points out a contradiction in the way David refers to the Messiah. This indicates what about Jesus' identity?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:44 shows that David calls the Messiah 'Lord,' indicating Jesus' superiority and divine status, thus revealing his identity as the Son of God.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus stated that the children of this world marry in Luke 20:34.
questions.explanation: In Luke 20:34, Jesus indeed states, 'The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage,' affirming this truth.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus claimed that God is a God of the dead in Luke 20:38.
questions.explanation: Luke 20:38 clarifies that God 'is not a God of the dead, but of the living,' thus the statement is false.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 20:38 teach about God's nature?
options: God is the God of the living, affirming the resurrection
God is impartial, showing no favoritism
God is the Creator of all things visible and invisible
questions.correctAnswer: God is the God of the living, affirming the resurrection
questions.explanation: Luke 20:38 states that God 'is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him,' affirming God's relationship to the living and the doctrine of resurrection.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does Luke 20:16 teach through the parable of the vineyard?
options: Unbelief and rejection of God's messengers lead to judgment
Sin is primarily a private moral failing
All humans are justified by works
God shows partiality based on ethnicity
questions.correctAnswer: Unbelief and rejection of God's messengers lead to judgment
questions.explanation: Luke 20:16 explains that the lord of the vineyard will destroy the wicked husbandmen who killed his son, illustrating judgment for rejecting God's messengers.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning resurrection and eternal life is taught in Luke 20:35?
options: Those worthy of resurrection neither marry nor are given in marriage
Marriage continues unchanged in the resurrection
Resurrection is only spiritual, not bodily
There is no resurrection after death
questions.correctAnswer: Those worthy of resurrection neither marry nor are given in marriage
questions.explanation: Luke 20:35 says that those accounted worthy of the resurrection 'neither marry, nor are given in marriage,' teaching a transformed state in the resurrection life.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jesus demonstrate in Luke 20:23 when he perceives the craftiness of his questioners?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:23 shows Jesus perceiving the craftiness behind the question, demonstrating his divine attribute of omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Luke 20:25 when Jesus instructs to 'Render therefore unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's, and unto God the things which be God's'?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:25 highlights God's sovereignty over all realms, distinguishing rightful authority between earthly and divine spheres.

questions.question: How does the parable of the vineyard in Luke 20:9-16 connect to the theme of God's judgment elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It prefigures the rejection of Christ and God's final judgment as in Isaiah's prophecies
It only illustrates agricultural practices with no theological weight
It contradicts the concept of God's mercy in the Psalms
It denies God's role as judge
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the rejection of Christ and God's final judgment as in Isaiah's prophecies
questions.explanation: The parable in Luke 20:9-16 connects to Isaiah's themes of vineyard judgment, symbolizing Israel's rejection of God's Son and the ensuing judgment.

questions.question: How does Jesus' teaching on resurrection in Luke 20:37-38 prepare for New Testament teaching about eternal life?
options: It affirms bodily resurrection and God's covenant faithfulness to the patriarchs
It denies the resurrection in favor of reincarnation
It teaches that resurrection is only metaphorical
It claims only angels will be resurrected
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms bodily resurrection and God's covenant faithfulness to the patriarchs
questions.explanation: Luke 20:37-38 references God's self-identification as God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, underscoring resurrection and covenant continuity, foundational for NT eternal life doctrine.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 20:4 and Luke 20:8 teach about Jesus' authority?
options: Jesus' authority is divine and not subject to human origin
Jesus' authority is granted by earthly rulers
Jesus refuses to claim any authority
Jesus' authority comes from John the Baptist
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' authority is divine and not subject to human origin
questions.explanation: In Luke 20:4 and 20:8, Jesus challenges the origin of John's baptism and refuses to reveal his authority's human source, implying divine origin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 20:42 and Luke 20:44 teach about Christ's identity?
options: Christ is both David's son and Lord, affirming his divine and human nature
Christ is merely a human descendant of David
Christ is only a prophetic figure without lordship
David was mistaken about Christ's identity
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is both David's son and Lord, affirming his divine and human nature
questions.explanation: Luke 20:42-44 quotes Psalm 110 showing David calls Christ 'Lord' despite being his son, teaching the dual nature of Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine about marriage and resurrection is taught by the synthesis of Luke 20:34-36 and Luke 20:27-33?
options: In the resurrection, earthly marriage ceases and believers become like angels
Marriage continues unchanged in the resurrection
Marriage is irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: In the resurrection, earthly marriage ceases and believers become like angels
questions.explanation: Luke 20:34-36 and 20:27-33 together teach that resurrected life is different from earthly life, with no marriage, and equality to angels.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Jesus' teaching in Luke 20:22-26 endorses political compliance over divine justice. What does the passage actually teach?
options: One must render to both earthly authorities and God their due, affirming a balance of duties
Jesus commands total submission to political powers regardless of justice
Jesus rejects any obligation to earthly government
Jesus advocates violent overthrow of Caesar
questions.correctAnswer: One must render to both earthly authorities and God their due, affirming a balance of duties
questions.explanation: Luke 20:22-26 teaches rendering to Caesar what belongs to him and to God what belongs to God, balancing earthly and divine responsibilities.

questions.question: What doctrine about religious hypocrisy is taught in Luke 20:47?
options: Scribes who exploit others and perform for show will receive greater damnation
Religious leaders are always righteous by office
Hypocrisy is excusable when done publicly
questions.correctAnswer: Scribes who exploit others and perform for show will receive greater damnation
questions.explanation: Luke 20:47 condemns scribes who devour widows' houses and make long prayers for show, warning of severe judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Jesus' parable in Luke 20:13-15 concerning the sending of the beloved son?
questions.explanation: Luke 20:13-15 shows the lord sending many servants and finally his beloved son, demonstrating God's longsuffering toward sinners.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about Jesus' teaching on the resurrection and divine identity is found in Luke 20:37-38 and Luke 20:34-36?
options: The resurrection affirms eternal life, transformation, and God as God of the living
The resurrection is symbolic and denies bodily life
God is only concerned with earthly life
questions.correctAnswer: The resurrection affirms eternal life, transformation, and God as God of the living
questions.explanation: Luke 20:37-38 and 20:34-36 together teach resurrection involves eternal life, transformation into an angelic-like state, and God's ongoing relationship to the living.

questions.question: How does Luke 20:41-44 prepare the audience for understanding Christ's messianic identity in the broader biblical narrative?
options: By highlighting the paradox of Christ as David's son and Lord, opening Messianic expectations
By denying David's role in Messianic prophecy
By asserting Christ's purely human lineage
questions.correctAnswer: By highlighting the paradox of Christ as David's son and Lord, opening Messianic expectations
questions.explanation: In Luke 20:41-44, Jesus challenges common Messianic understanding, preparing for recognition of his divine lordship alongside Davidic sonship.
